newsitem.title: UK: Dollar steady in Europe as market awaits US data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar steady in Europe as market awaits US data.

text.p: The dollar was firm against the mark and yen in Europe morning trade, although fluctuations were small as the market sought fresh incentive in the wake of the weekend's Group of Seven meeting.
Dollar sentiment was positive, but overnight Asian trade had been quiet due to a Tokyo holiday, and market operators were now looking to U.S. economic data due later today for direction.

While the dollar was clearly attractive in terms of fundamentals, there was wariness about driving it up rapidly since the G7 meeting on Sunday had warned against excessive volatility in currencies, analysts said.
"The bias for the dollar is still clearly higher, but the G7 has played its role here," said Klaus Baader, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.

"The overall environment is really unchanged in that the markets are beginning to get the feeling that policy-makers don't want the dollar to go much higher, and yet at the same time there are underlying attractions to the dollar," he said.

After trading in a very tight range against both the mark and yen overnight, the dollar was at 1.7315/19 marks and 126.73/83 yen at 0744 GMT, up from 1.7265/75 and 126.58/63 in late European trade on Monday.
Trading was expected to be fairly range-bound until the afternoon until the release of a series of U.S. economic data, which was due to continue throughout the week.

The focus for today would be the employment cost index (ECI) for the first quarter of 1997, since wage pressures were seen as a key ingredient in the Federal Reserve's decision on interest rates, analysts said. The Fed is due to hold its next policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meeting on May 20 amid expectations of a rate hike.
The first-quarter ECI is forecast to rise 0.9 percent after an increase of 0.8 percent previously.
The ECI is due to be released at 1230 GMT, at the same time as March durable goods orders data which were forecast unchanged from the previous month after a 1.5 percent increase in February.
The April consumer confidence index, due at 1400 GMT, was forecast at 118.4, almost unchanged from 118.5 previously.

Traders will also be keeping an eye on how U.S. stocks and bonds react to the indicators. Analysts said that although strong data would give the dollar a boost, it was not likely to be a huge one as the market was cautious about a dollar surge following the G7 meeting.

"Over the weekend we've seen something of a transformation in the German position; they seem even less accommodative towards a decline in the mark. So I think it will be a cautious upward move for the dollar," DMG's Baader said.
Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said at the G7 meeting that the U.S. wanted a strong, but not stronger, dollar, and that the G7 did not want an overshoot in currencies.
Meanwhile, the mark was lower against other European currencies due to dollar/mark's firmness in morning trade.
The British pound was firmer on the mark in line with the German currency's overall softness, while cable was steady.
Dealers said the market had mostly discounted a victory by Britain's opposition Labour party in Thursday's general election, and that sterling/mark was now mainly taking its lead from dollar/mark.
